executiveSummary: GM0175's official 2025 identity, contained reference point, 19,249-resident control, 46 neighbourhoods, eleven BAG places, 24 BRT settlements and six logical road-border links are coherent, and all ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Ommen is a large rural and recreation municipality around the Overijsselse Vecht, its Regge confluence, Ommerkanaal, villages, floodplain, wooded estates and Lemelerberg/Besthmenerberg nature. Water-management responsibility changes at Ommen: Waterschap Vechtstromen manages the Vecht toward the German border, while WDODelta manages water level and navigation downstream toward the Zwarte Water. Four fresh public Waterinfo point observations at audit time report Vecht and Ommerkanaal level/discharge, but they are observations rather than a T+72 footprint or warning. The simulator's canonical Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset selects neither Vecht nor Regge, yet reports an exact persistent 0.587381 m depth. With unchanged forcing, affected population changes from zero at T+24 to 454 at T+72 and burden from 69,286 to 277,870 person-hours. This is unsupported local precision; Vecht, Regge, Ommerkanaal, floodplain/defence, groundwater and rain/sewer pathways must remain separate. The municipal sewer programme says two thirds of sewers are still combined, heavy rain can overflow diluted wastewater, rural pressure sewers depend on pumps, some properties use resident-owned IBAs, and surface water/wadis provide storage. Wildfire is another reproducible contradiction. Current municipal/VRIJ evidence identifies about one third of Ommen as nature, Lemelerberg, Besthmenerberg, forest/heath, busy recreation, difficult access, mapped water points and a 60-farmer bosbrandweergroep with 30 tractor/tanker participants; those are planning resources, not guaranteed availability. A controlled source inside the 1,335 ha Buurtschap Lemele reports flame 0.222541, smoke 0.414596 and zero affected people, while the source ranks sixth behind sportpark Westbroek and unrelated northern neighbourhoods. Eight active single hazards reuse this same complete 46-neighbourhood order. Current municipal evidence also shows seasonal camping traffic deliberately routed around the busy centre and Hessel Mulertbrug; the long-running Junne bridge restriction moves heavy traffic to the Ommen or N36 crossings. The municipal-node graph cannot represent these internal Vecht crossings, north/south access, Ommen station/rail or destination-specific external care. Nearest listed 24/7 acute care is Saxenburgh Hardenberg, 12.45 km straight-line away. Public context supplies 277 full-resolution-assigned water assets, four Waterinfo observations, one large-user electricity-planning sample, provider polygons, 77 antenna sites, 20 schools and two government-service points, but no contained fixed KNMI, warning, RIVM air/care, NDW, seismic or Waterinfo forecast point. These do not supply live topology, occupancy, capacity, backup, passability, staffing or restoration. Exact first-72-hour hazard, service and recovery values must remain visibly synthetic or Unknown until incident forcing, dynamic recreation population, physical dependencies and confirmed actions/resources are bound; NoData is never zero, open, safe or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0175 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; CBS/PDOK CC BY 4.0 and BAG Public Domain Mark 1.0
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0175 as Ommen in Overijssel and Veiligheidsregio IJsselland, with 19,249 residents, density 107/km², 24.4% aged 65 or older and 2,555 one-person households. The reference point [6.466191932038979,52.52198345660154] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Forty-six neighbourhoods in eleven districts sum to 19,260 residents, eleven above the municipal control (+0.057%); households total 8,155 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 4,695. Deterministic allocation subtracts eleven without rewriting published observations.
Eleven BAG places and 24 BRT settlements—six woonkernen, sixteen buurtschappen and two gehuchten—are retained; no BAG place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.

Average home value and housing tenure/type fields have four null rows, cars per household thirteen, social/AOW/disability fields four each, and district heat/public charging all 46. Null is NoData, not numeric zero or service absence.

Large sparse rural/nature records such as Buurtschap Lemele (465 published residents/1,335 ha), Varsen (795/1,177 ha), Junne (85/1,065 ha) and Vilsteren (195/1,063 ha) require different hazard and transient-population evidence from compact Ommen neighbourhoods.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Programma Water en Riolering: sewer, rainwater, groundwater and surface-water roles
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal programme pages inspected 3 September 2026; policy/system context without a stated blanket reuse licence, live telemetry or fixed refresh cadence
supports: The municipality describes combined, separated and pressure sewers; approximately two thirds is still combined and can overflow diluted wastewater to ponds or ditches during cloudbursts.
Rural wastewater is transported over long distances by pumps/pressure mains, while some rural properties are not connected and use resident-owned and maintained individual treatment systems (IBAs).

Municipal surface waters and wadis provide storage, infiltration and delayed drainage. Rainwater is used to recharge groundwater and refresh surface water, while wastewater treatment remains a separate chain.

The climate programme identifies water nuisance, heat and drought stress-test bottlenecks intended for resolution by 2030 and periodic updating. A target, programme or stress test is not current asset state or event performance.
Municipality, Vechtstromen, WDODelta and regional partners hold different wastewater, urban groundwater/rain, surface-water, water-quality and defence roles; one service score cannot merge them.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat, Waterschap Vechtstromen and Waterschap Drents Overijsselse Delta
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Vecht/Regge/Ommerkanaal observations, authority boundary and high-water operations
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026 at 18:03 UTC, generally ten-minute CC0 observations; water-board pages dated 2024–2026 are observed/historic operating and static responsibility context, not the simulator event; water-board blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: At 17:30 UTC on 2 September 2026, Waterinfo reported Ommen Vecht level 261 cm NAP/discharge 3.15 m³/s and Ommerkanaal level 266 cm NAP/discharge 0.39 m³/s; all four were marked fresh and not possibly faulty, with the Vecht records classified normal. Point status is not a flood footprint, threshold, forecast or T+72 trajectory.

WDODelta states it manages Vecht water level and navigation from Ommen downstream to the Zwarte Water; Vechtstromen manages from Ommen toward the German border. Exact incident ownership can depend on location/mechanism.

A 30 May 2024 Vechtstromen observed event recorded high Vecht and Regge water after prolonged rain, saturated soil, pumps in operation and locally persistent drainage. A 3 July 2025 event closed Junne lock when high Vecht level made navigation unsafe.

Historic high-water operations used pumps, temporary pumps, sandbags and big bags, followed by inspections and repairs to weirs, pumps, dikes, defences and banks. These demonstrate action causality but are not guaranteed present resources or a current forecast.

No contained Waterinfo forecast point exists in the deployment snapshot. Observed normal point values at one instant never establish future safety, defence condition, absence of local flooding or service recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Current Ommen nature-fire prevention and response context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal/VRIJ article published 28 May 2026; current prevention/planning context, not an ignition, perimeter, forecast or incident resource commitment; reuse licence not stated
supports: The authority identifies Lemelerberg, Besthmenerberg, forests, heath and recreation areas, says roughly one third of Ommen is nature and notes heavy use by residents, recreationists and tourists during dry periods.

Nature fire and smoke can move quickly with wind; access requires current nature maps of usable routes and extinguishing-water points. People are told to leave toward public roads without blocking gates or access.

Ommen has a bosbrandweergroep network described as 60 farmers, thirty with tractors and slurry tanks, who know the area and can create wet zones. Published membership is preparedness context, not proof of incident-time availability, crew, fuel, water, route or dispatch.

A historic VRIJ Fire Bucket Operations exercise at landgoed Junne used the Junne weir as a water source and a woodland stopline with interregional/military resources; it is training evidence, not guaranteed T+72 capability.
Current location and response evidence contradict a source-insensitive wildfire map but does not provide live fuel moisture, wind, visitor count, ignition probability or suppression completion.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Recreation traffic, Hessel Mulertbrug and Junne crossing context
evidenceSources.edition: Camping-route notice dated 7 August 2024; current bridge/project pages inspected 3 September 2026; observed seasonal/planning infrastructure context, not live traffic or passability; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality calls Ommen a major Vechtdal tourist destination with many campgrounds and nature visitors. Seasonal camping traffic enters via N340, N348 and N48 and is deliberately routed to reduce centre and Hessel Mulertbrug congestion.

Municipal traffic planning treats the Hessel Mulertbrug and its approaches as a central crossing and is changing the north-side circulation. A project plan or historic count does not establish incident passability or throughput.

The bridge over Junne weir has been restricted against heavy/wide/high traffic since 2017. Published alternatives send affected traffic to the Ommen Vecht bridge about 6.5 km away or the N36 bridge about 8.5 km away, with different agricultural/heavy-vehicle eligibility.

The municipality's public Junne project record documents unresolved legal/technical planning and evolving vehicle restrictions. Its current exact operating state must be verified rather than inferred from an old proposal.
Campground count, route signs, bridge projects and static stops do not establish people present, vehicle supply, accessible evacuation, traffic control or emergency priority.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / PDOK, Provincie Overijssel, ProRail and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regional roads, Ommen station/rail and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026 and ProRail/OVapi deployment snapshots inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; CC0/CC0/best-effort/CC0 respectively
supports: Six logical NWB border links represent N48 and N36 toward Hardenberg, N341 toward Twenterand, N348 and N340 toward Dalfsen, and N347 toward Hellendoorn, each with 150 synthetic nominal units. Distinct corridors can still share local crossings/junctions and must not be read as live throughput.

Ommen station and 48 transit stop areas include several camping/recreation locations. ProRail geometry and GTFS schedules do not establish train/bus operation, ridership, vehicle/driver availability, emergency boarding or incident capacity.
The municipal-node graph does not encode Hessel Mulertbrug, Junne/N36 crossings, Vecht north/south subareas, rail/road structures, flood/smoke/tree state or campground last-mile access.

RIVM v1.1 lists no covered acute hospital inside GM0175. Nearest listed 24/7 acute care is Saxenburgh Medisch Centrum in Hardenberg, about 12.45 km straight-line from the municipal reference point, with acute obstetrics, nine rooms and 10,660 reported 2025 visits.
Static facility role does not establish route travel time, ambulance, staffing, occupancy, diversion, generator/fuel, clinical capacity or acceptance during an Ommen event.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Crisisplan 2023–2026 and first-72-hour preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Crisisplan 2023–2026 with addendum adopted 10 December 2025; current national 72-hour guidance inspected 3 September 2026; official doctrine/guidance, not a resource inventory or restoration promise; reuse licence not stated
supports: VRIJ defines incident-driven command, information, population care, evacuation/reception, medical, mobility and recovery responsibilities rather than a fixed automatic sequence.
Municipal acute population care and aftercare operate regionally, but the public plan does not provide current Ommen shelter sites, transport, staff, stock, accessibility, activation or completion.

Rijksoverheid asks households to prepare for the first 72 hours with three litres of water per person per day, food, medicines, information and backup power. Guidance is not observed household stock or an aid-arrival/restoration deadline.
Every decision and recovery change needs actor, request/confirmation, resource, place, valid/expiry time and completion; doctrine alone cannot calibrate service curves.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis, Netbeheer Nederland, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, RDI, DUO, KVK, KNMI, RIVM, Rijkswaterstaat and NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial water, utility, telecom, education, facility, weather and traffic context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026, CC BY-SA 4.0 and contributor-dependent; other deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026 with source-specific editions/licences
supports: Full-resolution municipality assignment retains 277 HWH objects: ten sewer pumps (three with non-null capacity), two sluices, 27 surface-water pumps (all with non-null capacity), one wastewater plant and 237 weirs. Managers include Vechtstromen/WDODelta and null fields; points do not establish compatible units, connectivity, state or backup.

One 7731PA sample maps to Enexis area RT Raalte and reports withdrawal 53.5/55.2 MW existing/required with 6.6 MW/54-request queue; injection is 53/82.6 MW with 15 MW/49 requests, thirteen projects and earliest 2026. This is large-user planning, not current load, reserve, outage or restoration.

At the reference point live public polygons return Enexis electricity/gas and Vitens water, but no drainage or media match. Provider-supplied Public Domain territory records were last updated 7 September 2025; point responsibility is not full-boundary connectivity or service state.

RDI retains 77 sites/165 antennas, DUO twenty education locations and KVK/PDOK two government-service points. Registers do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, occupancy, shelter role, staffing, supplies or opening.

Zero contained fixed KNMI observations/warnings, RIVM PM2.5/acute-care, NDW situations and seismic origins are scoped NoData. Four Waterinfo observations are positive context while zero contained forecast points remains NoData; neither means all-clear or guarantees future state.
